Subject: Request: retention exception and evidence for clinical tenant

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team liked the throughput numbers. We're now working with compliance to finish a small but time-sensitive ask before procurement will sign. Our regulator requires that audit traces driven by clinical workflows for our pilot tenant must be retained for 12 months rather than the platform default 90 days.

Specific asks: 
- Can Redwood provide a documented, scoped exception to the tenant-level log TTL for the Surgexa clinical tenant and the list of compensating controls you will apply?
- We need SOC 2 / SIG evidence showing the ingestion and retention controls, and a brief operational runbook we can include in our CAIQ response.

Attached is our SIG fragment that highlights the retention sections (Surgexa_SIG_questions_20281028.pdf). Procurement also asked for an indicative timeline for turning this on (and whether it requires a Dedicated or Private deployment).

We appreciate a short reply with next steps — Procurement would like to lock a go/no-go by COB Friday.

Best,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Security & Compliance
Surgexa Health

Thanks for the clear ask and for sending the SIG fragment. Summarizing our short answer up front: we can support a 12-month retention carveout for a single tenant under a scoped exception with controlled compensating controls and auditability. It does not automatically require Private deployment — we typically implement tenant-scoped retention windows on Dedicated or Hosted where capacity allows, but we'll confirm capacity/impact after you accept the operational terms below.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) We need a signed "Retention Exception Addendum" that defines the tenant ID(s), retention window, and proof-of-delete obligations. I can circulate a one-page addendum.
2) Priya (cc'd) will propose the implementation plan (storage, mask/redaction, sampling) and whether the change is a configuration flip or requires a dedicated pool.
3) Irene (cc'd) will map the SOC 2 / SIG artifacts we can provide and outline gaps that would require compensating controls.

I've attached a provisional evidence matrix and a skeleton addendum to speed procurement review (redwood_provisional_evidence_matrix_v1.xlsx). Please flag any sections in the SIG PDF that are blocking.

I'll aim to have the addendum drafted today so procurement has something to review.

Subject: RE: Request: retention exception and evidence for clinical tenant

Hi all —

Technical summary and constraints (high level):
- Implementation approach: tenant-scoped retention override layered on top of our existing ephemeral pipeline. We implement a shadow bucket per-tenant for longer windows; logs are routed via the same secure ingestion pipeline.
- Encryption/KMS: we can support either Redwood-managed KMS or a customer BYOK via a limited-scope KMS key (we'll need an integration window).
- Access controls: retained logs are placed in a role-separated store; access is restricted to an allow-list and every access is logged and forwarded to our immutable audit store for 5 years.
- Operational impact: ~12 months retention for a single production tenant increases storage by ~2.8x for that tenant's trace volume. On Hosted we can enable this provisionally for up to two tenants without Dedicated, subject to capacity planning and a short performance test. For sustained multi-tenant long retention (>=3 tenants) we recommend Dedicated.

Compensating controls we propose (must be accepted by Surgexa):
- Masking of PII at ingestion for non-essential fields (we will provide a field-level map).
- Quarterly sampling exports for Surgexa (signed delivery) to demonstrate proper retention and deletion windows.
- Scheduled evidence snapshots (SIG/SOC artifacts) and a joint runbook for proof-of-delete exercises.

I'll coordinate with infra for the performance test and provide a short SOW (1-2 pages) and an estimated schedule (we can be live with configuration flip and acceptance testing within 7-10 business days after addendum signature).

Priya Natarajan
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
